title: cairn-restart-cycles-the-system
why: Outline 5.3.4: "`cairn start` (= cairn cairn start) brings the system up: ground loop, bus, shims. `cairn stop` takes it down." Measured 2026-11-10: `cairn restart` answers "no such device or command"; the cycle exists only as the unit names (cairn-ground-loop, cairn-bus) and per-part verbs an operator must remember in order, often 300 miles from this box. Re-deriving that order each time is the defect Law 1 names.
how: One module beside the cairn device's code, cairn/devices/cairn/cycle.py, holds stop() and start(); three Python shortcuts in cairn/devices/cairn/bin/ call it (5.4.3.3, 5.4.3.4), and the launcher already runs them as `cairn start` (ticket 30366e99655a). The order is containment: the ground loop's pulse wakes shims and their mail wakes the bus (5.3.5.5), so stop takes the loop down first and then the bus (its shims go with its process); start wakes the loop and then the bus. Everything composed already stands: the loop's lock (guard.held) and record (heartbeat.read_record) name it, SIGTERM stops it promptly (ground_loop proof test_stop_is_prompt), shim.ensure_ground_loop wakes it, bus_client.remote.exchange speaks to the bus without waking it and remote.ensure_bus wakes it. Every home is read from HOME, so a scratch HOME cycles a scratch system.
traces_to: Law 1 -- the resolver is spent on the novel, not on re-deriving the settled; the safe cycle order is settled knowledge with no address. Also Law 4 -- while the order is prose and memory rather than a verb, it is a tracked debt, not a resting state.

clauses.claim: over a scratch HOME with nothing running, `cairn start` exits 0, and afterwards that HOME's ground loop lock is held and its bus answers stats
from up, `cairn stop` exits 0, and afterwards the loop lock is free and the bus does not answer; a second `cairn stop` exits 0 and its output says nothing was up
from up, `cairn restart` exits 0, and afterwards the bus answers with a pid other than the one before and the loop lock is held by a pid other than the one before
the live bus pid and the live ground loop pid are the same before and after the proof's every cycle: the verbs act only on the HOME they run under
the three shortcuts are Python scripts in cairn/devices/cairn/bin/, and cycle.py imports no other device's code (RULE 1)

constraints.text: 5.3.4 `cairn start` (= cairn cairn start) brings the system up: ground loop, bus, shims. `cairn stop` takes it down.
5.3.5.3 Restarting a shim never takes down the bus it once woke.
No, cairn restart does not restart the running cc instance(s).

intention: `cairn start`, `cairn stop` and `cairn restart` (long form `cairn cairn start|stop|restart`) bring the system up, take it down, and cycle it: the instance's ground loop and its one bus process, which holds every shim. Distinct from `cairn cc restart`, which relaunches a Claude Code session; no CC session is touched.

decisions.text: D1: cairn/devices/cairn/cycle.py: stop() SIGTERMs the pid the loop's record names while guard.held says the lock is held, waits up to 90 s for the lock to free (a beat in flight costs about 24 s), then sends the bus {op: shutdown} through remote.exchange when stats answers and waits up to 60 s for it to stop answering. start() clears a COMMAND_EXIT flag left at the loop home (it would end the new loop at its first beat), calls shim.ensure_ground_loop(), waits up to 60 s for the lock, then calls remote.ensure_bus(). Each prints one line per part (up, down, already down, still up) and returns 1 when a part is still in the wrong state after its wait (Law 7), else 0.

D2: cairn/devices/cairn/bin/start, stop and restart, each a `#!/usr/bin/env python3` script (mode 0755) that puts the repo root on sys.path and calls cycle: start(), stop(), and stop() then start() for restart; the exit code is the call's.

D3: the proof cairn/devices/cairn/proofs/test_start_stop_restart_cycle_the_system.py runs bin/cairn as a subprocess with HOME set to a scratch folder from the scratch door and CAIRN_GROUND_LOOP_UNIT and CAIRN_BUS_UNIT set to proof-named units, reads that HOME's loop lock and bus answer after each verb, reads the live bus and loop pids before and after, and stops whatever it started in its teardown. One tooth per clause.

out: the web server (5.3.4 names ground loop, bus and shims only)
help listing a device's class bin (cairn/tools/base bin_shortcuts, its own ticket)

measured.saw: `cairn restart` answered "no such device or command"; cairn/devices/cairn/bin/ did not exist
SIGTERM ends the loop promptly; exchange dials the socket and never spawns; ensure_bus and ensure_ground_loop are the wakers
